# azion_waf_rule_sets (Resource)

Authoritatively manages **every** exception (rule set) of a WAF.

The configuration is the complete list of the WAF's exceptions. On each refresh
the provider reads all of the WAF's exceptions from the API, so changes made
outside Terraform, in Azion Console for example, show up in `terraform plan`:

- An exception **created** outside Terraform is planned for deletion.
- An exception **deleted** outside Terraform is planned for re-creation.
- An exception **changed** outside Terraform is planned to be changed back, for
  every field the configuration declares.

`terraform apply`, including `terraform apply -auto-approve` in a pipeline,
restores the declared set. Rolling back means reverting the configuration and
applying again.

~> **Do not use `azion_waf_rule_sets` together with `azion_waf_rule_set` on the
same WAF.** Each would delete or recreate the other's exceptions on every apply.
Use `azion_waf_rule_set` when other tools or people are allowed to manage some of
a WAF's exceptions. Use `azion_waf_rule_sets` when Terraform must be the only
source of truth.

## Exceptions are keyed by name

Each key of `rule_sets` is the exception's name. Renaming a key deletes the old
exception and creates a new one. An exception renamed in Azion Console is treated
the same way: the new name is deleted and the declared name is recreated.

The API does not require exception names to be unique within a WAF. When it holds
several exceptions with the same name, the one Terraform already manages keeps the
name. Each of the others is keyed `<name>#<exception_id>`, appears in the plan
for deletion, and triggers a warning. Keys of that form are therefore reserved and
rejected in the configuration.

## Drift and enforcement

`active` defaults to `true`, so an exception disabled outside Terraform is
re-enabled on the next apply.

`rule_id`, `path`, `operator`, and the per-condition `name` and `value` are
refreshed from the API but **not** defaulted. A declared field that was changed
outside Terraform is reverted. An undeclared field keeps whatever value the API
holds, and updates send that value back unchanged. The reasons are the same as
for `azion_waf_rule_set`: a default `rule_id` would silently retarget the
exception, `operator` has no documented default, and the others are free-form.

The plan lists only the exceptions that change. Exceptions whose declared
fields match the API are left untouched.

Drift is only detected when state is refreshed. `terraform plan -refresh=false`
does not detect it.

## Adopting an existing WAF

Prefer importing (see below). Import reads every exception of the WAF into
state, so the first plan shows exactly what would change.

When the resource is created without importing:

- A WAF exception with the same name as a declared key is adopted and updated
  in place, not duplicated.
- Exceptions that are not declared are **left in place** by the first apply,
  with a warning, because that plan never showed them. They appear for deletion
  in the next plan. Declare them in `rule_sets` to keep them.

To migrate from `azion_waf_rule_set`, move each exception into `rule_sets`, then
remove the old resources from state without destroying them. Use a `removed`
block with `destroy = false` (Terraform 1.7+) or `terraform state rm`.

## Applying changes

The API has no batch endpoint, so changes are applied one exception at a time:
deletions first, then updates, then creations. If a request fails part of the
way, state records the exceptions that were already applied, and the next apply
finishes the rest.

Destroying this resource deletes **all** exceptions of the WAF.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# First, create the parent WAF
resource "azion_waf" "example" {
  result = {
    name   = "My WAF"
    active = true
  }
}

# Then declare every exception of that WAF. Exceptions not listed here are
# deleted on apply, including ones created in Azion Console.
resource "azion_waf_rule_sets" "example" {
  waf_id = azion_waf.example.id

  rule_sets = {
    "Allow health check" = {
      rule_id  = 0
      path     = "/health"
      operator = "contains"
      conditions = [
        {
          condition = {
            match          = "any_url"
            condition_type = "generic"
          }
        }
      ]
    }

    "Allow custom header" = {
      rule_id = 0
      conditions = [
        {
          condition = {
            match          = "specific_http_header_name"
            name           = "X-Custom-Header"
            condition_type = "specific_on_name"
          }
        }
      ]
    }

    "Allow trusted query string" = {
      rule_id = 0
      active  = false
      conditions = [
        {
          condition = {
            match          = "specific_query_string_value"
            value          = "trusted_value"
            condition_type = "specific_on_value"
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

### Removing every exception

```terraform
resource "azion_waf_rule_sets" "example" {
  waf_id    = azion_waf.example.id
  rule_sets = {}
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `rule_sets` (Attributes Map) Every exception of the WAF, keyed by exception name. An empty map deletes all exceptions. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rule_sets))
- `waf_id` (Number) The WAF identifier. Changing it replaces the resource.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Identifier of the resource. Same as `waf_id`.
- `last_updated` (String) Timestamp of the last Terraform update of the resource.

<a id="nestedatt--rule_sets"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rule_sets`

Required:

- `conditions` (Attributes List) Conditions for the WAF exception. Each item must contain a single `condition` object. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rule_sets--conditions))

Optional:

- `active` (Boolean) Whether the exception is active. Defaults to `true`.
- `operator` (String) The operator for the exception: regex or contains. Supplied by the API when not declared.
- `path` (String) Path pattern for the exception. Supplied by the API when not declared.
- `rule_id` (Number) The rule ID that this exception applies to. 0 means all rules. Supplied by the API when not declared.

Read-Only:

- `exception_id` (Number) The ID of the WAF exception.
- `last_editor` (String) Last editor of the exception.
- `last_modified` (String) Last modified timestamp.

<a id="nestedatt--rule_sets--conditions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rule_sets.conditions`

Required:

- `condition` (Attributes) A single condition for the WAF exception. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rule_sets--conditions--condition))

<a id="nestedatt--rule_sets--conditions--condition"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rule_sets.conditions.condition`

Required:

- `condition_type` (String) Type of condition: generic, specific_on_name, or specific_on_value.
- `match` (String) The match type for the condition.

Optional:

- `name` (String) The name for specific condition on name. Supplied by the API when not declared.
- `value` (String) The value for specific condition on value. Supplied by the API when not declared.

The valid `match` values for each `condition_type` are listed in the
[`azion_waf_rule_set` documentation](waf_rule_set.md#condition-match-types).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
terraform import azion_waf_rule_sets.example <waf_id>
```

Import reads every exception of the WAF into state.
